label: input j at a late original position (t >= 5)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is j during the original phase at position t >= 5 (orig_idx 5-8). It is fully token-specific: j makes up 99.97% of activations, other tokens appear only as 7 negligible activations (about 0.02 of max) at step 8, and every j at t >= 5 fires (precision 1.0). It never fires on j at t <= 4, at the delimiter, or during the copy phase, even when j is fed back as an input or is the output. Magnitude grows as <DEL> gets closer: the top activations (about 1.0 of max) are a j in the last original slot (to_go = 0), a j with to_go = 1 reaches about 0.6-0.65, and a j at t = 5 with several tokens still to come is about 0.3. Prior tokens, the first token, and repeats have no meaningful effect.

issues: The predicate is right. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.99993, F1 0.99996, mass recall 0.999998. The only misses are 2 activations at about 0.02 of max on non-j tokens at step 8, and there are 0 false positives. It never fires at the delimiter or in the copy phase (0 of 3.2M dev steps), and never on j at t<=4.

The magnitude claim in the explanation is wrong. Magnitude depends on the absolute position t, not on how close <DEL> is (to_go). Holding t=5 fixed, j with to_go=0 (L=6), to_go=1 (L=7) and to_go=3 (L=9) all look the same. Mass per firing is about 1.95e-5 in each case (0.0547/2801, 0.0548/2801, 0.0530/2714), and all of them sit only in activation quartiles 1-2.

Counterexamples from the dev profile. 'p f t z b y [j:0.66] <DEL>' has j at to_go=0, t=6, at 0.66 rather than the claimed ~1.0. 'z k x v p m 0 [j:0.76] <DEL>' has to_go=0, t=7, at 0.76. '3 i k m 1 [j:0.30] e <DEL>' has to_go=1, t=5, at 0.30 rather than the claimed 0.6-0.65. 'j w j h o 0 p [j:0.85] j' has to_go=1, t=7, at 0.85.

Quartile coverage by t shows a clean staircase. t=5 falls in quartiles Q1-Q2 (about 0.3 of max), t=6 in Q2-Q3 (about 0.6), t=7 in Q3-Q4 (about 0.75-0.85) and t=8 in Q4 (about 0.98-1.0). The top activations at to_go=0 are all L=9, t=8 cases. The explanation mistook this t effect for a to_go effect because t and to_go are confounded in the top examples.
The label itself, 'input j at a late original position (t >= 5)', is accurate and does not overclaim.
skeptic.revised_label: input j at original position t >= 5; magnitude rises with absolute position t (about 0.3 at t=5 up to about 1.0 at t=8) and does not depend on distance to <DEL>
